scope: Premise/quote inspection, duplicate and manifestation audit, and targeted fresh-search spot checks. Absence claims remain provisional.

decisions.notes: Strong evaluation-comparability question. Reframe from a direct contradiction to an unresolved construct-validity gap: end-to-end paper acceptance and scientific subtask correctness measure different things.
Near-duplicate of 3449d52437ae. The third source on human-versus-LLM ideation does not materially establish the central gap.
Useful controlled-scaffolding comparison. 'Direct contradiction' is too strong because task selection, baseline strength, models, budgets, and novelty definitions differ.
Potentially valuable benchmark-interoperability study. The reported percentages concern different tasks and denominators, so describe a comparability gap rather than contradictory measurements.
Cross-domain generalization is plausible and actionable. The AI Scientist source is contextual rather than evidence for HypoRefine's boundary; add domain-specific hypothesis-generation baselines.
Same cross-domain AI Scientist-v2 question as 7be9af90741e. The human ideation study is only tangential evidence.
Keep the domain-transfer question, but do not treat the Nature account and system paper as independent systems. Compare the architecture against domain-native agents and experimental modalities.
Substantively duplicates f549c8bdbc34.
Merge with the independent-validation card. Avoid claiming two independent passing manuscripts; the records describe overlapping systems/authors and differing review settings.

The two co-scientist records are manifestations/descriptions of the same underlying work, not independent evidence. ReplicationBench is from a different domain and does not make the proposed replication design minimal.

Independent replication of peer-review success is a clear, consequential target. Specify repeated blinded submissions, venue policy, reviewer composition, acceptance variance, and preregistered outcomes.
Premise incorrectly treats two records of the Google co-scientist work as independent systems. Robin does not rescue the proposed identical-benchmark comparison.

Benchmark interoperability is valuable, but do not require one literal pipeline containing all three artifacts. AstaBench already provides a broader benchmark suite; the sharper gap is whether rankings and failure profiles transfer across end-to-end generation, replication, and reproducibility evaluations.
Component mash-up without a demonstrated dependency or bottleneck. Combining three systems is not itself a field gap, and attribution would be poorly identified.
A clean modular intervention: replace an ideation stage while holding the downstream research pipeline fixed, then measure idea diversity, feasibility, execution success, and final evidence quality.

ReviewEval already compares MARG and AI Scientist review outputs against expert-relative criteria. The narrower remaining question is causal: what happens when these reviewer signals steer an end-to-end pipeline?

Keep as an AI Scientist-specific learning-loop question. Broader claims that no feedback-learning evidence exists are outdated; recent lab-in-the-loop and automated-review systems provide adjacent evidence.
Same upstream feedback-learning question as 4f1dba767eeb.
Same feedback-loop question. Preserve expert-versus-LLM disagreement as one experimental condition in the canonical card.

Benchmark-guided online adaptation is testable, but frame it as a general intervention rather than requiring these exact three systems. Compare fixed-agent evaluation with evaluation-feedback adaptation under held-out tasks.

fresh_search_findings.finding: AstaBench already aggregates several scientific-agent evaluations and weakens broad claims that benchmark unification is wholly absent.
ReviewEval directly compares MARG and AI Scientist reviewers on expert-relative review dimensions, partially addressing the review-consistency premise.
CycleResearcher uses automated review to improve automated research, so broad no-review-feedback-loop claims are no longer tenable.
A 2026 lab-in-the-loop study reports controlled evidence that experimental feedback can improve an AI scientist agent, further narrowing broad feedback-loop gaps.
